headline: Oracle cuts 21,000 jobs in 12 months, 13% of workforce, citing AI adoption
summary: Oracle's 21,000 job cuts highlight a growing trend: tech giants reporting record revenues while reducing staff, often citing AI as a factor for both growth and workforce reductions.
details: Oracle announced a reduction of 21,000 employees over the past 12 months, a 13% decline in its workforce. The company explicitly stated in a financial regulatory filing that "The adoption and deployment of AI technologies across our operations have resulted, and may continue to result, in reductions to our workforce."

This revelation adds to a growing trend in the tech industry where companies report record revenues while simultaneously cutting jobs. AI is frequently cited as both the engine of growth and the reason for these workforce reductions, with tech layoffs reaching a multi-year high in May.

GitLab, for instance, laid off approximately 350 workers (14% of its staff) in June 2026 to fund AI infrastructure investment and manage surging traffic from AI workflows. CEO Bill Staples noted a "generational rebuild" of core infrastructure to support 100x growth requirements, involving exiting 22 countries and flattening management layers.

Google has also been quietly cutting employees across its Cloud division, including cybersecurity staff, even as Cloud revenue grew 63% to exceed $20 billion. These cuts have occurred through rolling performance reviews, voluntary buyouts, and reorganizations, with estimates for 2026 ranging from 1,500 to over 3,000 engineers.

Intuit announced plans in May 2026 to eliminate roughly 3,000 jobs, about 17% of its total workforce. This restructuring aims to reduce complexity and reallocate resources toward AI-focused initiatives, as communicated by CEO Sasan Goodarzi to staff.

Meta also laid off about 8,000 employees, roughly 10% of its workforce, around the same time. While 7,000 employees were moved into new AI-focused roles, CEO Mark Zuckerberg stated the cuts were necessary because "success isn't a given" in AI.

Cisco announced nearly 4,000 job cuts, about 5% of its workforce, despite reporting better-than-expected profit and revenue. CFO Mark Patterson clarified that this was not a savings-driven restructure but a realignment of resources around silicon, optics, security, and AI.

Cloudflare cut about 20% of its workforce (1,100 people) in May 2026, reporting its highest single quarterly revenue in company history. CEO Matthew Prince indicated that the majority of those laid off were "measurers," referring to middle management, finance, legal, and internal auditing roles.

General Motors eliminated 500 to 600 jobs, primarily in IT roles, in May 2026, citing a reevaluation of workforce needs amid uncertain market conditions. While AI played a role in the decision, it was not the sole reason, as GM stated it was "transforming its Information Technology organization."

headline: Only 17.7% of 117,854 AI agent skills are graded for security, 1 in 32 is unsafe
summary: A new report reveals that nearly 97,000 AI agent skills remain unaudited, with significant risks lurking in the long tail of less popular tools. Installing an agent skill can expose your shell and sensitive data.
details: A security analysis of 117,854 AI agent skills reveals that only 17.7% are popular enough to be graded. Among these graded skills, 1 in 32 (3.1%) is found to be unsafe or rejected, posing a significant risk to users.

The primary concern isn't just the unsafe skills, but the vast majority that remain unchecked. Installing an AI agent skill or MCP server grants untrusted code access to your shell, environment variables, and even the agent's own configuration and memory.

The analysis used a rule-based scanner, modeled on SlowMist's Agent Security Framework, to perform static checks on READMEs and code. It identifies patterns like data exfiltration, credential harvesting, reading sensitive files, and privilege escalation.

While popular skills are generally safer, the danger lies in the obscure, less-audited repositories often found when searching for niche tasks. This 'long tail' represents approximately 97,000 skills that are effectively unaudited.

Beyond classic shell risks, a new attack surface involves agent config and memory theft. Skills can read your agent's configuration, stored context, and credentials-by-proxy, a threat model often overlooked by current directories.

AgentSkillsHub provides a trust layer, showing each skill's security grade (safe, caution, unsafe, reject) and specific red flags. Users can check any skill before installation and filter out unaudited or unsafe options.
